question: You arrive at a road accident and the scene is safe. What is the correct first action in the primary assessment of an unresponsive casualty?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Compressions come later — you must first check for danger, then assess responsiveness, then open the airway and check breathing before deciding on CPR.

answers.text: Shout for help and call emergency services, then open the airway by head-tilt chin-lift and check breathing for up to 10 seconds

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. After confirming the scene is safe and the casualty is unresponsive, the primary survey follows D-R-A-B-C: call for help, open the Airway, check Breathing, then respond to Circulation.

answers.text: Place the casualty in the recovery position straight away

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The recovery position is used only once the casualty is breathing. An unresponsive casualty must first be assessed for breathing before positioning.

answers.text: Apply a tourniquet to control any visible bleeding before doing anything else

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Life-threatening haemorrhage control is part of the primary survey, but Airway and Breathing assessments come first in the standard DRABC sequence.

overallFeedback.feedback: Remember the DRABC sequence: after confirming Danger and checking Response, open the Airway and look-listen-feel for Breathing before acting on Circulation.
Well done. The DRABC primary assessment sequence — Danger, Response, Airway, Breathing, Circulation — is the foundation of all first-aid management.
